claims.claim: Computing/computer science is the systematic study of algorithmic processes that describe and transform information, including their theory, analysis, design, efficiency, implementation, and application.
An algorithm is a computable set of steps to achieve a desired result.

Computer science is defined by Wikipedia's summary of the field as the study of computation, information, and automation, spanning theoretical areas (algorithms, theory of computation) and applied ones (hardware and software design, AI, HCI).

Major subfields include theory of computation, algorithms and data structures, programming languages and formal methods, computer architecture, operating systems, networks, databases, artificial intelligence, human-computer interaction, computer graphics, and security/cryptography.

Computer science and software engineering are separate but complementary disciplines; David Parnas characterized CS as studying computational properties in general and software engineering as designing specific computations for practical goals.

Study of computer hardware belongs largely to computer engineering, and commercial deployment/maintenance of systems falls under information technology or information systems, distinguishing both from computer science.

The remark 'computer science is no more about computers than astronomy is about telescopes' is commonly attributed to Edsger Dijkstra and conveys that the computer is an instrument while computation is the object of study.
Computer science combines mathematical rigor with empirical investigation; Newell and Simon (1975) characterized it as an empirical discipline, and the field draws on theory, experiment, and design.

Because an algorithm is language- and machine-independent, its correctness and efficiency can be reasoned about before any implementation, and complexity conclusions hold across every machine that runs it faithfully.

Worked example: linear search inspects up to n entries in the worst case, while binary search on a sorted list of ~1000 items reaches an answer in at most about 10 comparisons (ceil(log2(1000)) = 10).

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether computer science is fundamentally a science, a branch of mathematics, or engineering.
positions: Newell and Simon: an empirical discipline (a science)
Denning and others frame computing as drawing on all three: theory, experiment (abstraction/modeling), and design
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson presents CS as combining mathematical rigor and empirical testing, and notes the debate rather than asserting a single verdict.
